site.title: Neuro-Oracle: A Trajectory-Aware Agentic RAG Framework for Interpretable Epilepsy Surgical Prognosis
titleLines: Neuro-Oracle: A Trajectory-Aware Agentic RAG Framework
site.description: Neuro-Oracle encodes pre-to-post-operative MRI change as a 512-dimensional trajectory vector, retrieves similar historical cases, and grounds an interpretable epilepsy surgical prognosis in them with a quantized Llama-3-8B agent.
site.keywords: Epilepsy Surgery, Surgical Prognosis, Longitudinal MRI, Siamese Network, Supervised Contrastive Learning, Retrieval-Augmented Generation, Agentic RAG, Large Language Models, Llama-3, FAISS, EPISURG, Interpretability, AAAI 2026 Fall Symposium Series

abstract.title: Abstract
abstract.body: Predicting post-surgical seizure outcomes in pharmacoresistant epilepsy is a clinical challenge. Conventional deep-learning approaches operate on static, single-timepoint pre-operative scans, omitting longitudinal morphological changes. We propose Neuro-Oracle, a three-stage framework that: (i) distils pre-to-post-operative MRI changes into a compact 512-dimensional trajectory vector using a 3D Siamese contrastive encoder; (ii) retrieves historically similar surgical trajectories from a population archive via nearest-neighbour search; and (iii) synthesises a natural-language prognosis grounded in the retrieved evidence using a quantized Llama-3-8B reasoning agent. Evaluations are conducted on the public EPISURG dataset (N=268 longitudinally paired cases) using five-fold stratified cross-validation. Since ground-truth seizure-freedom scores are unavailable, we utilize a clinical proxy label based on the resection type. We acknowledge that the network representations may potentially learn the anatomical features of the resection cavities (i.e., temporal versus non-temporal locations) rather than true prognostic morphometry. Our current evaluation thus serves mainly as a proof-of-concept for the trajectory-aware retrieval architecture. Trajectory-based classifiers achieve AUC values between 0.834 and 0.905, compared with 0.793 for a single-timepoint ResNet-50 baseline. The Neuro-Oracle agent (M5) matches the AUC of purely discriminative trajectory classifiers (0.867) while producing structured justifications with zero observed hallucinations under our audit protocol. A Siamese Diversity Ensemble (M6) of trajectory-space classifiers attains an AUC of 0.905 without language-model overhead.

blocks.body: All experiments use EPISURG, a public collection of 430 T1-weighted MRI scans from epilepsy surgery patients; 268 subjects have both a pre-operative and a post-operative scan. Because the public release contains no per-patient Engel seizure-freedom scores, each subject receives a binary proxy label derived from surgery type. Temporal procedures, including lobectomy, lesionectomy, and multilobar temporal resections, are labelled y = 0 (favourable outcome proxy, cited seizure-freedom rate 65–70% at two years), while purely extra-temporal (frontal, parietal, occipital) resections and hemispherectomy are labelled y = 1 (less-favourable outcome proxy, cited rate 40–55%). The cohort comprises 215 subjects with y = 0 and 53 with y = 1, a ratio of roughly 4:1. Each post-operative scan is rigidly registered (6 DOF) to its pre-operative scan with ANTsPy; both volumes are then z-score normalised and centre-cropped or zero-padded to a 128 × 128 × 128 grid at 1 mm isotropic resolution. Deformable registration is deliberately avoided, since non-linear warping would smooth the localised volume changes the model aims to capture.

Proxy-label caveat. Because the label follows resection type and every model sees the post-operative scan, the networks may learn the anatomy of temporal versus non-temporal resection cavities rather than subtle epileptogenic pathology, in effect predicting surgery type instead of seizure outcome. All reported metrics therefore measure proxy-label recovery, not clinical seizure-freedom prognosis. Neuro-Oracle should be read as an architectural proof-of-concept, designed to be readily applicable once per-patient outcome registries become available.

blocks.alt: Neuro-Oracle in three phases: trajectory encoding with a shared 3D ResNet-50, trajectory retrieval from a FAISS population archive, and agentic RAG prognosis with Llama-3-8B-Instruct
blocks.caption: Figure 1. Overview of the proposed Neuro-Oracle framework. (i) Pre- and post-operative MRI pairs are registered and encoded through a shared 3D Siamese ResNet-50 backbone. (ii) The morphological difference is projected into a compact trajectory vector, which is used to retrieve historically similar cases from a population archive. (iii) A quantized LLM reasoning agent evaluates the retrieved evidence to synthesize a transparent, natural-language surgical prognosis.

items: Contrastive trajectory encoding. A weight-shared 3D Siamese ResNet-50 encodes the pre-operative scan and the rigidly co-registered post-operative scan. An MLP head projects their feature difference to a 512-dimensional, ℓ2-normalised trajectory vector Δv. The encoder is trained with an equal-weight sum of Supervised Contrastive loss (temperature τ = 0.07) and Focal Loss, the latter countering the 4:1 class imbalance.

Population archive and retrieval. The frozen encoder embeds every training subject, and the resulting unit-norm vectors are stored in a FAISS exact inner-product index (IndexFlatIP), so the inner product equals cosine similarity. For each query, the k = 5 most similar historical trajectories are retrieved.

Calibrated LLM reasoning agent. The query profile and the retrieved neighbours (age, sex, outcome) form a structured prompt for a 4-bit NF4 quantized Llama-3-8B-Instruct, which is instructed to set aside matches with an age gap above 15 years and to answer SUCCESS or FAILURE with a one-sentence justification. The final probability blends the neighbour vote with the LLM verdict as pOracle = 0.60 × pneighbor + 0.40 × pLLM, where pneighbor is the fraction of retrieved neighbours with y = 1 and pLLM is 0.20 for a SUCCESS verdict and 0.80 otherwise. A case is assigned y = 1 when pOracle exceeds the default threshold of 0.50.

sections.title: Experimental Setup
sections.body: All methods are evaluated with five-fold stratified cross-validation (seed 42), which preserves the 4:1 class ratio in every fold. For each test fold, an independent encoder is trained on the other four folds, and the FAISS index is rebuilt from that split's non-augmented training subjects only, so no test subject or augmented sample ever enters the retrieval pool. Seven methods are compared on the same 268 subjects: two static single-timepoint baselines trained on the post-operative scan, ResNet-50 (M1) and 3D-ViT (M2); four classifiers on frozen trajectory vectors, namely logistic regression (M3), a 2-layer MLP (M3b), cosine k-NN (M4), and the Siamese Diversity Ensemble (M6), an equal-weight soft vote over ExtraTrees, two MLPs, and a calibrated RBF-SVC; and Neuro-Oracle (M5). AUC-ROC is the primary metric, and F1, sensitivity, specificity, and balanced accuracy are secondary. All metrics are computed on the union of the five held-out folds, which covers each subject exactly once.

blocks.body: Trajectory-based classifiers (M3–M6) reach substantially higher sensitivity on the minority class than the static ResNet-50 baseline (M1, 0.396), suggesting that the longitudinal difference encoding carries signal absent from a single scan (Table 1). Among them, Siamese + Logistic Regression (M3) attains the highest sensitivity (0.849) and the Siamese Diversity Ensemble (M6) the highest AUC (0.905). The static 3D-ViT baseline (M2) is nonetheless competitive, with an AUC of 0.867 and the highest balanced accuracy (0.871). Neuro-Oracle (M5, AUC 0.867) matches M2 and Siamese + k-NN (M4, AUC 0.868) while also producing a natural-language justification for every prediction (Figures 2 and 3).

blocks.alt: ROC curves of six methods on EPISURG under 5-fold stratified cross-validation, with AUCs from 0.793 (ResNet-50 Static) to 0.883 (Siamese + LogReg)
blocks.caption: Figure 2. ROC curves for six baseline and proposed methods under 5-fold stratified CV on EPISURG (N=268); Siamese Diversity Ensemble (M6) is omitted for visual clarity. AUC values are reported in Table 1.

blocks.alt: Aggregated 5-fold confusion matrix of Neuro-Oracle (M5): 198 true negatives, 17 false positives, 23 false negatives, and 30 true positives
blocks.caption: Figure 3. Aggregated confusion matrix for Neuro-Oracle (M5), 5-fold stratified CV. Rows: ground-truth proxy label (0=temporal resection, corresponding to Success / Engel I; 1=non-temporal or complex resection, corresponding to Failure / Engel II-IV); columns: predicted label. M5 achieves specificity of 0.921 and sensitivity of 0.566 at the default threshold.

blocks.body: Threshold optimisation chiefly benefits Neuro-Oracle (Table 2). At its optimised threshold of 0.34, sensitivity rises from 0.566 to 0.698 while specificity falls only from 0.921 to 0.916, lifting balanced accuracy from 0.744 to 0.807: markedly fewer less-favourable outcomes are missed at the cost of a marginal rise in false positives. Siamese + k-NN (M4) keeps the same operating point at its optimum of 0.42, and M3 and M3b retain 0.50.

blocks.caption: Table 2. Threshold-optimised performance. Threshold selected via grid search over [0.30, 0.50] (step 0.02), maximising balanced accuracy on aggregate held-out predictions. M3 and M3b retain τ = 0.50 as optimal.

blocks.body: Replacing the trained encoder with a random, untrained one reduces performance to near chance (AUC 0.488), confirming that the learned trajectory vectors carry genuine discriminative signal (Table 3). Restricting retrieval to k = 1 lowers AUC to 0.741, showing the benefit of multi-neighbour vote smoothing. Removing the age-gap filter leaves AUC, sensitivity, and balanced accuracy unchanged, consistent with the moderate age variance in EPISURG; the filter's role is to improve the coherence of the agent's reasoning rather than the discriminative score. Figure 4 further contrasts input modality and reasoning engine: relative to the single-scan k-NN reference (0.793), switching to the trajectory Δv (0.868) or to the Llama-3 agent (0.867) raises AUC, and the full pipeline (0.867) preserves this level while adding clinical reasoning.

blocks.caption: Table 3. Ablation study of Neuro-Oracle pipeline components (N = 268, 5-fold stratified cross-validation).

blocks.alt: Bar chart of AUC-ROC: single scan with k-NN 0.793, single scan with Llama-3 0.867, trajectory with k-NN 0.868, and trajectory with Llama-3 (Neuro-Oracle) 0.867
blocks.caption: Figure 4. AUC-ROC across input modality and reasoning engine combinations. Single scan with k-NN achieves 0.793; switching to longitudinal trajectory Δv (0.868) or using a Llama-3 reasoning agent (0.867) individually increase performance. The full Neuro-Oracle pipeline (Trajectory Δv + Llama-3) preserves the high performance of the geometric embedding and generates interpretative clinical reasoning. The chance level AUC=0.5 is shown as a dashed red line.

blocks.body: Table 4 summarises embedding and retrieval quality. A mean top-5 cosine similarity of 0.919 indicates that queries typically find close neighbours in the archive, in line with the compact clusters visible in Figure 5. Top-5 retrieval fidelity reaches 83.0%, and the calibration MAE of 0.189 reflects the inherent uncertainty of predicting a proxy label from geometric features on an imbalanced cohort.

blocks.caption: Figure 5. t-SNE projection (perplexity = 30, 2000 iterations) of the 512-dim ℓ2-normalised trajectory vectors for all 268 EPISURG subjects. Green circles show proxy label y=0 (temporal resection, corresponding to Success / Engel I in legend); Red circles show y=1 (non-temporal or complex resection, corresponding to Failure / Engel II-IV).

blocks.text: Interpretability Audit of the LLM Agent

blocks.body: An audit of the raw Llama-3-8B-Instruct outputs records an age-filter adherence of 73.9% and a zero-hallucination rate of 100.0%. No reply contained information beyond the supplied context, which reflects the tightly structured prompt rather than an inherent capability of the language model, and the agent followed the age-reasoning rule in most, though not all, cases. Both rates are research audit measures and should not be read as guarantees of clinical safety.

sections.title: Limitations and Future Work
sections.body: The cohort of 268 subjects is too small to yield confidence intervals narrow enough for strong claims about pairwise method differences, and all subjects come from a single centre, which limits conclusions about cross-site and cross-scanner generalisation. Future work should link EPISURG scans to de-identified Engel outcome registries under ethical approval, evaluate cross-centre generalisation on independent cohorts, and examine whether supervised fine-tuning of the quantized agent on outcome-labelled clinical notes improves the fidelity of its reasoning.
